name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,326

entries.clue: Manage to get round small group of trees (5)

indicatorNotes.to get round: COPE goes round the next letter, holding it inside

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

annotation.surface: Someone struggling to walk all the way round a little wood.
annotation.walkthrough: S sits between the P and E of COPE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thicket of small trees or undergrowth, often cut back for timber.

entries.clue: Halved cash with street players (4)

indicatorNotes.Halved: only half of the next word is kept

blocks.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street

annotation.surface: Buskers splitting their takings down the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests street performers sharing money; 'players' is really the definition, a play's actors.
annotation.definitionFit: The theatre sense: the actors taking part in a production, taken together.

entries.clue: Standard king’s garden open to the public (4)

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm
K is the chess abbreviation for king

annotation.surface: A royal garden that anyone may now walk in.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of king's reads as 'king is' joining the pieces, or simply the surface's possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: public grounds laid out with grass and trees for anyone to use.

entries.clue: I bite idly resolving fitness for consumption (9)

indicatorNotes.resolving: re-solving the letters: working them out into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone nibbling absent-mindedly while deciding whether the food is safe to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is a neat fit for the surface: idle biting is exactly how one tests edibility.
annotation.definitionFit: Edibility is the quality of being fit to eat.

entries.clue: Tedium of moving bedroom (7)

annotation.surface: The dreary business of shifting house, one bedroom at a time.
annotation.walkthrough: BEDROOM and BOREDOM share exactly the same seven letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Boredom and tedium both mean weariness from dullness.

entries.clue: Run into coastal shore as breakers do (6)

indicatorNotes.into: R is put into the next word

blocks.note: a beach is the shore of the coast
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

annotation.surface: Waves racing up onto the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition describes an action: waves (breakers) breach a sea wall, so the answer is a verb, what breakers do.
annotation.definitionFit: Breakers breach defences, breaking through them.

entries.clue: Renegade and traitor, primarily (3)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take what comes first in each word

blocks.note: first letters of Renegade, And, Traitor

annotation.surface: A description of a turncoat.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a rat is a renegade and traitor.
annotation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side.

entries.clue: Monstrous biocidal bats (8)

indicatorNotes.bats: batty, crazy: the letters go mad

annotation.surface: Horror-film bats that kill every living thing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bats' reads as a noun, the creatures, but works as an adjective meaning crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: Diabolic means devilish, monstrously wicked.

entries.clue: Combative Italian dividing his city over time (8)

indicatorNotes.dividing: IT splits the next word in two
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, sitting over the next piece: it comes first

blocks.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: A quarrelsome Italian causing division in his home town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back to the Italian, so his city is an Italian one: MILAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Militant means aggressive, ready to fight.

entries.clue: Leaders among sharks and rays eat fish (7)

indicatorNotes.Leaders among: the leading letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of sharks, and, rays

annotation.surface: The big sea predators feeding on smaller fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like the thing eaten in the surface; it is the definition, and 'eat' gives DINE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the young pilchard, a small oily sea fish often sold tinned.

entries.clue: Follow around river path (5)

indicatorNotes.around: TAIL goes around the next letter

blocks.note: to tail someone is to follow them
R is the map abbreviation for river

annotation.surface: Directions for a walk: go along the riverside path.
annotation.walkthrough: R sits after the T of TAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: A trail is a path, especially through countryside.

entries.clue: Suffering minutes inside club, mostly loud (10)

indicatorNotes.inside: M goes inside the next word
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for minutes
FORTE (loud, in music) minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Enduring a few minutes in a nightclub where the music is far too loud.
annotation.walkthrough: Forte is the musical term for loud. 'Club' suggests a weapon or society; here it is a disco.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: physical or mental unease, a milder word for pain.

entries.clue: Route maps ordered for Cheddar perhaps (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the answer by what it uses: a trap baited with cheese

indicatorNotes.ordered: the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone ordering road maps before a trip to the English village of Cheddar.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a Somerset village as well as the cheese, so the surface reads as travel planning; the cheese is the bait a mousetrap is for.
annotation.definitionFit: A mousetrap is typically baited with a piece of cheese such as Cheddar.

entries.clue: Weapon armistice nearly knocked for six (8)

indicatorNotes.nearly: not quite all: drop the last letter
indicatorNotes.knocked for six: sent flying, so the letters scatter

annotation.surface: A truce that almost collapsed, with weapons drawn again.
annotation.walkthrough: To knock something for six is to hit it hard, a cricket phrase for a shot clearing the boundary.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the curved single-edged sword of the Middle East is one kind of weapon.

entries.clue: Totally striking, OK? (8)

annotation.surface: A remark that something is completely stunning, seeking agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like impressive but means on strike.
annotation.definitionFit: The adverb sense, as in 'rejected outright': completely, with nothing held back.

entries.clue: Company briefly employing family member (6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: drop the last letter

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

annotation.surface: A firm taking on a relative for a short spell.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is nepotism; 'briefly' seems to limit the job but cuts USING.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the child of an aunt or uncle is one of your relations.

entries.clue: Swelling British association of workers (6)

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British

annotation.surface: A British trade union growing in size.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swelling' reads as an adjective about membership, but is the noun definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A bunion is a painful swelling on the big toe joint.

entries.clue: Bot making all get grief on Tinder initially (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: making all get grief on Tinder
blocks.note: first letters of making, all, get, grief, on, Tinder

annotation.surface: An automated account on a dating app that upsets everyone it matches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bot' looks like a software robot; it is the larva of the botfly, a kind of maggot. Tinder is a dating app.
annotation.definitionFit: A bot is the maggot-like larva of the botfly.

entries.clue: Sign of hesitation after my remark upset reveller (10)

indicatorNotes.after: ER comes after the other piece
indicatorNotes.upset: the letters are knocked over into a new order

blocks.note: er is what you say when hesitating

annotation.surface: A partygoer hesitating after an offensive remark.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the reveller was upset by the remark; 'upset' is really the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A merrymaker is someone joining in festivities, a reveller.

entries.clue: Want chessplayer to sacrifice bishop (4)

indicatorNotes.to sacrifice: give up a piece, as in chess: the B goes

blocks.note: one of the two sides in chess is Black
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; it is removed

annotation.surface: A chess player wanting to give up a bishop as a gambit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as desire, but here means need or shortage.
annotation.definitionFit: Want and lack both mean a shortage of something.

entries.clue: Tackle illicit drugs (4)

blocks.note: the noun: equipment, as in fishing tackle
a slang term for illegal drugs

annotation.surface: An instruction to deal with the drug problem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' is a verb in the surface but the noun equipment in the answer; fishing gear and the dealer's slang for drugs share the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Gear means equipment, and in slang, drugs.

entries.clue: Mean drunk in snug (5)

blocks.note: close-fitting, as a garment can be

annotation.surface: A nasty drunk sitting in a pub's snug.
annotation.walkthrough: In fact three definitions: snug fits TIGHT too. A snug is a small cosy room in a British pub, which sets the drinking scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Tight means stingy, drunk, and close-fitting.

entries.clue: Bond regularly involved in strife (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals: the letters are taken at an even spacing, every second one
indicatorNotes.involved in: the letters are found within the next word

annotation.surface: A James Bond film plot: the spy caught up in conflict.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy; it is the definition, a link or tie.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a link that holds people together, as in family ties.

entries.clue: Rubbish clothing at start of season (7)

indicatorNotes.at start of: GARB is placed at the start of the next piece

blocks.note: a season, like an age, is a period of time

annotation.surface: Awful new fashions appearing at the start of the season.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start of season' tempts a solver to take S, but nothing else then fits; 'season' is a stretch of time, an era.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and the usual North American word for household waste.

entries.clue: Climb-down on the subject of free entertainment? (7)

blocks.note: a treat is entertainment paid for by someone else

annotation.surface: Backing down on a promise of free entertainment.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is the letter-heading word for 'regarding'.
annotation.definitionFit: A retreat is a climb-down, a backing away from a position.

entries.clue: Certainly cutting for each card game (5)

indicatorNotes.cutting: OK cuts into the next word, splitting it

annotation.surface: Someone cutting the deck before each hand of cards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' is a card-game word in the surface, but here it means going into.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the betting game of bluff played with five-card hands.
